about: Stages and settings for the weekly triage playbook. scripts/handoff.py reads this file: the stages it tracks and the outcomes each stage can record. The other keys are read by the assistant following SKILL.md. Each key is explained under notes.

stages.name: briefing
stages.do: Build the Monday briefing for the last 7 days, with its health alerts and its three things to do this week.

stages.name: explain
stages.do: Explain the week's big revenue, conversion or order value change, with ranked causes and the skill or playbook for each.

skip_when.reason: the briefing shows no big change to explain.

notes.look_ahead_days: Days after today that still count as this week when listing the other runs: on a Monday, 6 reaches Sunday. Step 0 passes today plus this many days to handoff.py list --today, so a read-out or confirm due on Thursday shows as due.
notes.max_problems: The most problems the triage hands off in one week. More than this and none get done: the rest wait for next week's briefing.
notes.playbook_for: Which playbook starts, or resumes, for each kind of problem. These are skill names; the playbooks are separate skills, so when one isn't installed, name the stage skill the briefing or the explain stage linked instead.
notes.playbooks: Each playbook's title, product and stages in order. A stage names the skill that does it, whether that skill writes, what to do, the outcomes it can record, product (revenue-anomaly-explainer covers Discovery: status suggests skipping it when the run has no Discovery account) and skip_when (suggest skipping when another stage had one of these outcomes). Picking the problems isn't a stage: no skill does it, so the playbook does it from the stages' results and the list of runs.
